title: The Dirac Information Carrier for Relativistic Quantum Computation
abstract: Quantum computation has traditionally been formulated by postulating abstract information carriers and subsequently identifying physical systems that realize them. We adopt the opposite viewpoint and ask what computational structure is supplied by a fundamental relativistic quantum system itself. Focusing on the simplest nontrivial massive spin carrier, spin-1/2, we show that its relativistic description supplies a native four-dimensional information carrier through the Dirac equation. The resulting Dirac information carrier possesses an intrinsic positive- and negative-energy decomposition that induces a physics-constrained computational structure comprising sector-preserving and sector-coupling quantum logic. Restricting the relativistic computational structure to the positive-energy sector and taking the nonrelativistic regime recovers the familiar Pauli qubit description. We distinguish mathematical unitary transformations from physically admissible gates and show how charge-conjugation structure, charge superselection, and associated reference-frame resources can constrain quantum logic beyond the sector-preserving structure. Finally, under appropriate physical assumptions, we establish the conditions under which this structure supports full single-carrier controllability. Our work establishes the Dirac information carrier as the massive spin-1/2 instance of a broader programme in which computational structures are derived from the relativistic representation carried by the underlying physical system.
summary: This work rethinks quantum computation by deriving its computational structure from the relativistic description of a massive spin-1/2 particle (the Dirac carrier). It shows that this intrinsic structure imposes limitations on possible quantum gates, distinguishing between mathematical symmetries and physically realizable operations. Ultimately, it provides necessary and sufficient conditions for achieving full control over this fundamental information carrier.
main_problem: The paper addresses how computational structure can be derived intrinsically from a fundamental relativistic quantum system, rather than assuming abstract carriers first.
main_result: It establishes the Dirac information carrier as a source of a constrained quantum logic (sector-preserving and sector-coupling gates) whose full controllability requires specific physical resources beyond simple unitary transformations.
method: The analysis uses group theory applied to the symmetry algebra ($\mathfrak{su}(4)$) governing the spin-1/2 system, distinguishing between mathematical unitaries and physically admissible quantum logic gates.
model_or_system: The model is the massive spin-1/2 particle described by the Dirac equation. The resulting information carrier is termed the 'Dirac ququart,' possessing an intrinsic positive- and negative-energy decomposition ($H_+ \oplus H_-$).
key_observables: Admissible quantum logic gates, sector coherence, and controllability conditions.
important_parameters: Mass ($m$), momentum ($\vec{p}$), and the structure of the Poincaré representation.
main_assumptions: The core assumption is that computational structure must arise from the intrinsic symmetries dictated by relativistic field theory (Dirac equation).
figures_summary: Not specified in the notes, but the mathematical flow involves mapping generators from $	ext{Spin}^+(1, 3)$ through the Dirac carrier to $SU(4)$.
paper_structure: The paper first derives the intrinsic computational structure from the positive/negative energy decomposition of the Dirac equation. It then analyzes the symmetry group ($SU(4)$) and defines physically admissible gates. Finally, it uses group theory (normalizers) to determine the necessary conditions for achieving full single-carrier controllability.
why_interesting: It provides a rigorous theoretical framework linking fundamental particle physics symmetries (Dirac equation) directly to the constraints on quantum computation, offering a physical basis for gate sets beyond abstract assumptions.
